reasons: Candidate layouts are not a global optimality proof.
Tile changes are conservatively charged as whole immutable tile versions and roots as flat reference tables.
Synthetic motion, source sizes and access profiles are preregistered analytical inputs rather than observed production distributions.
The model excludes allocator fragmentation, compressed-source decode workspace, latency, CPU, energy, thermal and physical-device pressure.
ImageCraft animation source remains dirty and unpublished and Fovea does not consume it as a production animation revision.

interpretation: Persistent tiles materially improve the extreme sparse case but do not establish a general default. At the 32 MiB/eight-frame point only four of 112 cases are feasible, representing uniform and tail-hot access for the same SPARSE-2048-256 encoded-source strategy at 32- and 64-pixel tiles.

The best retained candidate is 64-pixel tiles with every frame rooted: about 25.98 MiB retained, one-frame replay, and about 57.98 MiB conservative modeled peak. The 32-pixel candidate retains about 28.98 MiB and peaks near 61.01 MiB.

No reference-policy candidate for full-frame, half-canvas, moving-ball, mixed previous/source, or repeated previous-disposal scenarios fits the retained budget. No feasible reference candidate fits the 32 MiB Fovea hard cap after adding a materialized output and conservative working/root scratch.

The matrix is a deterministic candidate-family search, not a proof that every tile layout is impossible. Nevertheless, it rejects persistent tiles as a universal default and retains them only as a possible sparse specialization pending a lower-peak implementation and physical-device evidence.

The next general candidate should reduce retained state beyond full tile granularity or use independently validated compressed checkpoint state; any candidate must preserve the owned straight-alpha exactness and separate-default fail-closed boundary.
objective: Evaluate immutable persistent tile versions with shared checkpoint roots after retained full-canvas checkpoints failed the 32 MiB/eight-frame reference policy.

candidateFamilies: fixed intervals one through replay bound
scope.rootAccounting: flat eight-byte tile-reference table plus 64-byte header per retained root; unchanged tile versions shared
